articles.title: Is Cooper Flagg alright? Latest on Dallas Mavericks forward’s injury after an awkward fall on the floor
articles.summary: Cooper Flagg left the Dallas Mavericks’ 121-105 win over the Indiana Pacers on Friday night after a hard foul sent him crashing to the floor in
articles.body: Cooper Flagg left the Dallas Mavericks’ 121-105 win over the Indiana Pacers on Friday night after a hard foul sent him crashing to the floor in Indianapolis. Aaron Nesmith was called for a flagrant 1 while trying to stop a breakaway dunk, and a scuffle followed. Flagg landed on his left shoulder and did not play the second half. The team is calling it soreness. Coach Dusty May could not say whether an MRI is coming, only that Dallas would know more in a couple of days. He had 14 points in 17 minutes before it happened.What happened to Cooper Flagg?Cooper Flagg had just stolen the ball and was heading the other way for a dunk. Pacers’ Aaron Nesmith chased from behind and tried to block the attempt, and Dallas’ reigning Rookie of the Year came down awkwardly on the same shoulder he injured as a rookie. The foul was ruled a flagrant 1.Naji Marshall went straight at Nesmith under the basket. P.J. Washington joined him, Pascal Siakam and Ivica Zubac pulled Nesmith away, and Daniel Gafford tried to keep the peace. After a replay review, the officials gave double technicals to Nesmith and Marshall. Two Mavericks players also drifted off the bench, though May believed both were only checking on Flagg.Flagg split the two free throws and kept rubbing the shoulder as he walked to the locker room. Dallas led by 33 at the time.Another brief scuffle broke out near midcourt in the second half. However, there were no penalties. Pacers coach Rick Carlisle pointed out that Indiana has now been in multiple scuffles across its first two games.Flagg finished with 14 points, five rebounds, six assists, three steals and a block, and he was on pace for his first triple-double of the season. Two nights earlier, he scored 32 against Houston, the most ever by a teenager in a season opener, though Dallas lost 128-110. Nesmith had nine points on 2-of-7 shooting.Cooper Flagg’s latest injury statusThe Mavericks list the injury as left shoulder soreness. May said Flagg will be evaluated over the next couple of days, and he saw the forward in the locker room in good spirits. On the MRI question, May did not commit. “We’ll know in the next couple days what’s next,” he said.May also spoke kindly of Nesmith, whom he has known since high school, and called the play unfortunate.Flagg did not speak to reporters after the game. The word soreness can be read as encouraging, but his history with the same shoulder is why the evaluation matters. No MRI result or return timeline has been announced.Dallas hosts the San Antonio Spurs on Saturday, Oct. 24, at 8 p.m.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Un Doncic de otra galaxia (52+8+10) aúpa a los Lakers en Utah
articles.standfirst: El esloveno firma su décimo partido en la NBA con 50 o más puntos y el encuentro 63 con más de 40 puntos. Austin Reaves (29), otra vez su mejor lugarteniente
articles.summary: El esloveno firma su décimo partido en la NBA con 50 o más puntos y el encuentro 63 con más de 40 puntos. Austin Reaves (29), otra vez su mejor lugarteniente
articles.body: Apenas tres días después de que el polémico Draymond Green dijese que Doncic nunca ganaría el MVP de la NBA, el esloveno se encargó de cerrarle la boca firmando una actuación antológica en el triunfo de los Lakers en cancha de Utah Jazz (123-132) que mantiene a los angelinos invictos y como líderes en la Conferencia Oeste. Tras un primer cuarto en el que los Lakers desafinaron más de la cuenta en ataque y chirriaron en defensa, se vieron 18 puntos abajo ante los Jazz (47-28), parecía avecinarse una noche complicada para los angelinos. Pero Luka Doncic cambió esa percepción echándose a su equipo a la espalda, como tantas y tantas veces, y tomándose la remontada como un asunto personal. El esloveno acometió su propósito con decisión, empleó todo su talento ofensivo y no paró hasta conseguirlo. Acabó con 52 puntos (9/12 t2, 8/18 t3 y 10/11 tl), 8 rebotes, 10 asistencias y 2 recuperaciones en 38 minutos en cancha. Se convirtió así en el primer jugador en la historia de los Lakers en registrar 50+ puntos, 10+ asistencias, 5+ rebotes y 5+ triples en un solo partido. Fue una actuación sideral, otra más en su carrera. En su octava temporada en la NBA es la décima vez que anota 50 puntos o más. Y el partido número 63 en el que anota al menos 40 puntos. Así forjan su leyenda los mitos. El triunfo de los Lakers no fue sólo cosa de Doncic. Sin su lugarteniente favorito, Austin Reaves, no hubiese sido posible la remontada. El escolta, por el que Luka presionó en las oficinas de la franquicia angelina en verano para que renovasen su contrato, le secundó con 29 puntos (3/7 t2, 4/5 t3 y 11/13 tl). Poca participación por lo demás de Walker Kessler (2+7), Ziaire Williams (11) y Matisse Thybulle (11). En Utah Jazz, que cosechó su segunda derrota en tres partidos, los mejores fueron Lauri Markkanen (28+6), Keyonte George (24+9+10), Jaren Jackson Jr. (20) y Ace Balley (17+12+4). Todos ellos contribuyeron para que su equipo llegase con ventaja hasta que faltaban poco más cuatro minutos para la conclusión (116-113). Fue entonces cuando Doncic, que ya por entonces llevaba 41 puntos, apareció para poner la guinda a su formidable actuación anotando 11 puntos para enterrar las opciones de los Jazz. Primero anotó un triple para empatar (116-116 a 4.06). Poco después anotó dos tiros libres para adelantar a sus Lakers (116-118 a 3.34). A 2.22 metió otro triple para distanciar a su equipo (119-124) y puso el broche de oro a su recital anotando otro triple definitivo a 1.42 del final con el que coronó su obra de arte y abrochó el triunfo de su equipo (121-127). Los genios son así.

articles.title: Luka Dončić scores 52 points as Lakers improve to 3-0 with win over Jazz
articles.summary: Dončić became the third player in Lakers history to score 50 or more points with 10 assists in a single game, joining Elgin Baylor and Jerry West.
articles.body:
Luka Dončić scored 52 points for the Los Angeles Lakers in a 132-123 win over the Utah Jazz on Sunday, reaching the 50-point mark for the 10th time in his NBA career.

Dončić also nearly recorded a triple-double, adding eight rebounds and 10 assists. He shot 17 of 30 from the floor, including 8 of 18 on 3-point shots, and made 10 of 11 free throws.

In his third season with the Lakers, Dončić became the third player in franchise history to score 50 or more points and dish out 10 assists in a single game, according to The Athletic's Law Murray .

The last Lakers player to do it was Elgin Baylor on Feb. 13, 1963 against the Boston Celtics. Baylor also achieved the feat on Dec. 13, 1961 versus the St. Louis Hawks, while Jerry West joined him in a Jan. 21, 1962 game with the Cincinnati Royals.

Perhaps more important for the Lakers is winning their first three games of the season. After allowing 47 points to Utah in the first quarter, Los Angeles appeared to be on its way to its first defeat. Trailing 47-29 after the opening 12 minutes, the Lakers outscored the Jazz by 21 points in the second quarter for a 74-71 halftime lead.

Dončić scored 25 points in the first half, eight of them in the second quarter, while Austin Reaves added 10.

In the third quarter, Dončić added another 14 points and the Lakers needed every one of them to keep up with Utah. His 3-pointer with 2.1 seconds remaining in the frame put the Lakers ahead 103-100 going into the fourth.

The Jazz took a 111-110 lead midway through the quarter after going on a 13-1 run. After two Lauri Markkanen free throws put Utah ahead by three points, Dončić swished a 3-pointer to tie the score and then drew a charge on Keyonte George. He followed with two free throws after a Darryn Peterson foul to give the Lakers the lead and they held on to it for the remainder of the game.

A 3-pointer from Reaves was the dagger with 33.8 seconds left in regulation. Dončić added two free throws to seal the win with 12.3 seconds remaining.

Reaves finished with 29 points, shooting 4 of 5 on 3s. Collin Sexton added 13 off the bench, while Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams each scored 11 points.

Markkanen led the Jazz with 28 points, followed by George, who nearly reached a triple-double with 24 points, 9 rebounds and 10 assists. Jaren Jackson Jr. added 20 points, followed by Ace Bailey with 17 points, 12 rebounds and 4 assists for Utah, which dropped to 1-2.

Up next for the Lakers is a home matchup with the Portland Trail Blazers (2-0) on Tuesday.

articles.title: Jalen Williams Injured, Latest on Thunder Star After Gruesome Leg Injury
articles.summary: Oklahoma City Thunder star Jalen Williams suffered what appeared to be a gruesome leg injury after landing awkwardly following a dunk during Sunday's matchup against the Los Angeles Clippers.
articles.body:
Oklahoma City Thunder star Jalen Williams suffered what appeared to be a gruesome leg injury after landing awkwardly following a dunk during Sunday's matchup against the Los Angeles Clippers.

He was taken off the court on a stretcher after suffering the injury (Warning: Video contains a graphic injury) :

"I don't even know. I just feel bad for him," an emotional Shai Gilgeous-Alexander said during an postgame interview. "Nothing more than that. ... It's obviously gonna be tough without a player like that. But he's not gone forever, he'll be back better than ever and we know it. We've just gotta hold the fort down until he comes back."

If Williams' injury is as bad as it looked, however, it's possible his season is over.

"Those are tough man," head coach Mark Daigneault told reporters after the game regarding the injury. "We're not doing great. That's tough on the guys. Everyone empathizes, I think both teams, in those situations. But yeah, not doing great."

The 25-year-old came into Sunday's game averaging 16.5 points, six rebounds and 2.5 assists per game, shooting 38.7 percent from the field and 37.5 percent from three.

His 2025-26 season was also marred by injuries. He appeared in just 33 games during the regular season due to wrist and hamstring issues and only appeared in five playoff games, a major factor in the Thunder failing to get past the San Antonio Spurs in the Western Conference Finals.

But he's clearly one of the pillars of the organization alongside SGA and Chet Holmgren, which was solidified in July 2025 when the Thunder signed him to a five-year rookie max extension worth up to $287 million.

Unfortunately, staying on the court has been a struggle since. With Williams, the Thunder are arguably the favorites to win the NBA title yet again. Without him, those odds worsen.

articles.title: Magic guard Jalen Suggs helped off floor after leg injury in win over Knicks
articles.summary: Jalen Suggs' knee buckled hard as he tried to go up for a layup on Sunday night at Madison Square Garden.
articles.body:
Orlando Magic guard Jalen Suggs was helped off the court Sunday night after he suffered what appeared to be a significant non-contact knee injury.

Suggs, in the fourth quarter of the Magic's 111-102 win over the New York Knicks, went up for what should have been an easy fast-break layup at Madison Square Garden. But as Suggs went up, his right knee buckled hard.

Suggs fell to the ground awkwardly after missing the shot, and immediately reached for his knee while rolling around in pain underneath the basket.

Suggs remained down for quite some time. He was eventually helped up and limped off the floor to the locker room with his arms around others while barely putting any weight on his leg.

Magic head coach Sean Sweeney said he spoke with Suggs after the game, via NBA reporter Darko Dželetović , and that he was in "good spirits." Further specifics on Suggs' injury are not yet known, though he'll undergo further testing Monday.

Suggs finished the night with 4 points, 6 rebounds and 6 assists. The former Gonzaga star, who the Magic selected with the No. 5 overall draft pick in 2021, is in his sixth season in the league. He averaged 13.8 points and 5.5 assists per game last season while helping the Magic reach the playoffs for a third straight year.

The injury was the second significant one throughout the league on Sunday. Oklahoma City Thunder star Jalen Williams went down with a gruesome leg injury in OKC's win over the Los Angeles Clippers, and he had to be stretchered off the floor .

Despite losing Suggs, the Magic held on to grab the nine-point win Sunday. That marked their first victory of the season after they dropped back-to-back games to start the 2026-27 campaign. The Knicks fell to 0-3 with the loss.

While Suggs' status is still unclear, the non-contact nature of his injury is undoubtedly concerning for the Magic. With Paolo Banchero already sidelined with an ankle sprain, losing Suggs for any significant amount of time will make things much more difficult for the team as the new season gets started.

articles.title: 76ers deny Joel Embiid's push to play in back-to-back games, rest him during loss to Pistons
articles.summary: Joel Embiid dropped a triple-double on Saturday night in the 76ers' win over the Bucks.
articles.body:
Joel Embiid's pressure campaign didn't work.

The Philadelphia 76ers sat their star big man on Sunday in their 106-93 loss to the Detroit Pistons due to right foot plantar fasciitis management. The contest is the team's first back-to-back of the season, following Saturday's 127-116 win over the Milwaukee Bucks.

Embiid appeared to know this decision was coming, too, and he tried to get out in front of it.

"I actually want to play tomorrow, so can you guys put pressure on them?" Embiid said on Saturday night, via ESPN's Kris Rhim . "... I want to play tomorrow, so start writing articles and put pressure on them so they'll let me play."

It was a good effort, but the 76ers' brass wasn't swayed. Based on Embiid's injury history, and the fact that Sunday's contest is just the Sixers' fourth of the season, it's easy to understand why.

Embiid hasn't played in more than 40 games in a single season since the 2022-23 campaign, and he's averaged only 49 games a season in his decade in the league. He played in only 38 last season due to a knee injury, an oblique injury and more.

At this stage in Embiid's career, his health is something the 76ers have to work hard to manage. So far this season, he's been great. Embiid recorded the 10th triple-double of his career Saturday night in the 76ers' win over the Bucks with 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists. He helped Philadelphia get off to a 3-0 start, including a season-opening win over the defending champion New York Knicks.

The 76ers also ruled VJ Edgecombe, Dominick Barlow, Jabari Walker and Tacko Fall out for Sunday's contest due to various injuries, leaving them short at the position. Walker left Saturday's win early with a left knee issue. And without them available, the Pistons held on late to grab the 13-point win.

Regardless, the 76ers clearly aren't willing to push Embiid to play in back-to-back contests when they don't have to. Now, Embiid will have to keep trying to plead his case as the season moves on.

articles.title: Jalen Williams suffers gruesome leg injury, stretchered off court in Thunder's victory over Clippers
articles.summary: Williams suffered the injury after going up for a dunk late in the fourth quarter.
articles.body:
Oklahoma City Thunder guard Jalen Williams was taken off the court on a stretcher after suffering a significant leg injury near the end of Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Clippers.

Williams was fouled going up for a dunk and landed awkwardly with his left leg appearing to crumple underneath him. Williams' left foot was bent unnaturally and a Thunder staffer quickly covered it with a towel.

Some of Williams' teammates, including Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, became emotional and knelt over as Oklahoma City's medical team attended to Williams.

Williams eventually gave the crowd a thumbs up after he was placed on the stretcher. Fans gave Williams a standing ovation and chanted, "J-Dub," in support as he was wheeled out.

The Thunder did not have an immediate update on Williams' condition or the specifics of his injury.

Kris Dunn, who hit Williams as he came down from the dunk, was called for a flagrant 1 foul by the referees. Gilgeous-Alexander took the two flagrant free throws on Williams' behalf.

After OKC's 108-101 victory , Gilgeous-Alexander teared up during his postgame interview on the court.

"I just feel bad for him," Gilgeous-Alexander said of his longtime OKC teammate. "Nothing more than that."

Thunder head coach Mark Daigneault echoed that sentiment during his postgame news conference, saying he had no updates on Williams.

"Those are tough, man. We're not doing great," Daigneault said, via Daily Thunder's Brandon Rahbar . "That's tough on the guys."

Williams missed a significant chunk of last season due to various injuries, including a hamstring injury that kept him out of multiple games in the Western Conference finals. He played in just 33 games last season.

"I have no doubt in my mind that he'll be back and be better than he was before, just like how he handled the last couple of injuries," Gilgeous-Alexander told The Oklahoman's Justin Martinez . "It's unfortunate, his luck so far, but he's equipped for it. He's a warrior."

The Thunder also lost Cason Wallace and Jaylin Williams to injuries during Sunday's game. Daigneault said the team would have updates on their conditions Monday.

articles.summary: Jalen Williams was wheeled off the court during the closing minutes of Oklahoma City Thunder's win over the Los Angeles Clippers; Shai Gilgeous-Alexander was among the players visibly upset by the injury to Williams' lower left leg
articles.body:
Williams - a shooting guard who entered Sunday having averaged 18 points per game in his first 250 NBA contests - has been an All-Star and an All-NBA player already in his career, was a huge part of the Thunder team that won the 2024-25 NBA title.

He injured his lower left leg and saw his ankle turn in an unnatural angle in a drive with 1:14 remaining, with Williams immediately treated by medical personnel after going down underneath the basket on the Thunder's offensive end.

Williams' ankle was draped by towels before a stretcher was brought out, with players left visibly shaken by the incident and the game stopped for around five minutes before the Thunder completed their victory.

"Just feel bad for him," Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander said in a post-match interview, fighting back tears as he spoke. "Nothing more than that."

Williams, seated up on the stretcher, saluted the cheering fans with two thumbs-up signals as he was wheeled off the court.

There was no immediate diagnosis from the Thunder, though it was clear that the injury was severe - and the stretcher was called for within just a few seconds of the play ending.

Oklahoma City coach Mark Daigneault said the team would be briefed Monday morning with the latest updates on Williams' condition.

"Our whole city will have JDub in our thoughts and prayers as he deals with this adversity and as he makes his way through his recovery," Oklahoma City Mayor David Holt posted on social media after the game.

Williams missed 49 games last season with an array of issues, mostly hamstring problems and recovery from a significant surgery on his right wrist.

"He just loves playing, loves the competition," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "That's who he is. It's unfortunate, his luck so far. But he's equipped for it."

articles.title: Denis Bouanga and Leo Walta rescue LAFC in El Trafico thriller to secure MLS Cup playoff spot
articles.summary: LAFC secured their place in the MLS Cup Playoffs following a dramatic 2-2 draw against rivals LA Galaxy. Interim boss Xavi Tamarit praised his side's resilie...
articles.body:
LAFC secured their place in the MLS Cup Playoffs following a dramatic 2-2 draw against rivals LA Galaxy. Interim boss Xavi Tamarit praised his side's resilience as Denis Bouanga inspired a stunning second-half comeback after falling two goals behind in El Trafico.

LAFC secure playoff spot in derby thriller

LAFC have booked their place in the MLS Cup Playoffs following a thrilling 2-2 draw with the LA Galaxy at BMO Stadium. The hosts fought back from a two-goal deficit to salvage a crucial point in the latest edition of El Trafico.

Joseph Paintsil had put the Galaxy in complete control after capitalising on defensive errors to score twice. However, LAFC responded immediately with a quickfire double to rescue their postseason ambitions. The result guarantees LAFC a fifth consecutive playoff appearance. It also marks their eighth postseason qualification in just nine seasons.

Tamarit praises dramatic second-half fightback

Interim head coach Tamarit was thrilled by the fighting spirit shown by his players. His team had dominated stretches of the first half but found themselves trailing before conceding again early in the second. Despite the defensive setbacks, the hosts rallied impressively to rescue the match.

"I am very proud about the team, how we overcame in a really difficult situation that we didn't deserve," Tamarit told reporters. "They never give up."

The comeback was sparked by Bouanga, who pounced on a rebound after Galaxy goalkeeper JT Marcinkowski spilled Armindo Sieb's shot. Leo Walta then levelled the match following a dangerous cross from Heung-min Son.

While the comeback was commendable, LAFC were left frustrated by the manner of the goals they conceded. Paintsil's second strike came after Hugo Lloris spilled a shot from Erik Thommy, highlighting their defensive frailties.

Defender Aaron Long was critical of the backline, describing both Galaxy goals as "a little cheap, a little easy." He added: "Scoring two goals at home, that should be a win."

LAFC will now turn their attention to securing a higher seed with just two regular-season matches remaining. A strong finish is essential if they are to earn a coveted home fixture in the upcoming playoffs. In their final two matches, LAFC will face Minnesota United on November 2, and then, six days later, they will travel to take on the Seattle Sounders.

Tyrese Maxey encabezó a los Sixers con 29 puntos y James aportó 18. Los Sixers perdieron por primera vez después de arrancar con tres victorias al hilo. A diferencia de su remontada contra Cleveland, los Sixers encadenaron varias canastas para meterse en el partido, pero nunca tomaron la delantera. James, de 41 años, de vuelta en la alineación después de no jugar contra los Bucks para descansar la espalda, se abrió paso para conseguir tres bandejas consecutivas como parte de una racha de 9-0 que ayudó a los Sixers a recortar la diferencia a 56-44 al descanso. articles.title: 6 Terrible Contracts NBA Teams Wish Would Disappear
articles.summary: After a long, contentious negotiation, Jalen Duren finally landed a $200 million deal, but the Detroit Pistons were hesitant to max out their All-NBA/All-Star.
articles.body:
After a long, contentious negotiation, Jalen Duren finally landed a $200 million deal, but the Detroit Pistons were hesitant to max out their All-NBA/All-Star.

Long-term contract negotiations are a complex dance: Teams worry about luxury taxes and aprons, but also fear losing talent if they don't offer enough.

Many deals become significant miscalculations that teams wish they could remove from their salary-cap books through an amnesty provision, as the 2011 collective bargaining agreement allowed for eligible contracts. The longer and uglier the deal, the harder it is to move.

Those contracts can limit flexibility and shorten the championship window for former MVPs. Recently, teams have offered shorter contracts with less guaranteed money. Still, the damage is done in the following cases.

Didn't the Milwaukee Bucks re-sign Gary Trent Jr. to a four-year, $64 million contract?

Fresh off a season averaging 8.1 points per game, the 27-year-old wing got a deal that confused most competing executives.

With the Bucks retooling after trading Giannis Antetokounmpo to the Miami Heat, that heavy an investment in Trent is difficult to justify based on his projected contributions over the next four seasons.

Trent can shoot. He can play 20 minutes a game, but he's been a near-minimum player the last few years. The size of the raise is difficult to justify, and his contract could age poorly.

Immanuel Quickley and Jakob Poeltl, Toronto Raptors

The Toronto Raptors brought Kawhi Leonard back in a trade from the LA Clippers, costing several first-round picks. The Raptors have struggled recently to build a contender while working around the tax and first apron. The team returned to the playoffs after a three-year absence, and Leonard will make Toronto better when he's healthy.

The challenge is the $97.5 million owed to Immanuel Quickley over three years at a flat rate of $32.5 million. He's productive when he plays, but he's struggled with durability.

Similarly, Jakob Poeltl is due up to $104 million over four years, depending on incentives. His final season is partially guaranteed, but there has been little trade interest in the Raptors' oft-injured center.

Jamal Shead and Collin Murray-Boyles provided steady production. With Scottie Barnes and Leonard earning almost $92 million next season, Toronto has way too much invested in Quickley and Poeltl.

The Dallas Mavericks have too many forwards. From Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg to recent trade acquisitions Santi Aldama and Zaccharie Risacher, the Mavs don't have the budget for PJ Washington, the second-highest-paid player on the team behind Kyrie Irving.

Washington is in the first year of a four-year, $88.8 million extension. The Mavericks also drafted Morez Johnson Jr., re-signed Moussa Cisse, and re-signed Dwight Powell. Washington is better suited elsewhere on a contender, where he'd fit in as a complementary role player.

While his $19.8 million salary isn't outrageous this season, the length and total value of his contract could make him difficult to trade.

Since their 2022-23 championship, the Denver Nuggets have struggled to keep their roster together around MVP Nikola Jokić.

Following the departures of players such as Michael Porter Jr., Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Peyton Watson, even a core featuring Jokić, Jamal Murray and Aaron Gordon has been unable to take Denver back to the NBA Finals.

The Nuggets hoped Christian Braun, their No. 21 pick in 2022, would take on a larger role. His five-year, $125 million rookie-scale extension begins this season with a $21.6 million salary.

Unfortunately for Denver, Braun played just 44 games last season, and his three-point shooting dropped from 39.7 percent in 2024-25 to 30.1 percent.

Given the open looks Jokić creates, the Nuggets need Braun to space the floor reliably. Their financial commitment to him could become a major obstacle if he doesn't improve this season.

Should De'Aaron Fox be on the list, as the starting point guard of the San Antonio Spurs squad that advanced to the NBA Finals?

But then, the Spurs may not have known how quickly Dylan Harper would emerge as a powerful rookie contributor.

Fox is the team's highest-paid player this season, earning $49.5 million and with almost $222 million due over four years. All-Star Victor Wembanyama jumps from $16.8 million to about $43 million in 2027-28, and standout guard Stephon Castle will be right behind him with an extension due before the 2028-29 campaign.

Fox, who turns 29 in December, is signed into his early thirties. He shot just 31 percent from three-point range in 2025-26 and made several costly decisions in the NBA Finals against the New York Knicks.

While Fox shouldn't be the scapegoat for the Spurs' loss, he was brought in from the Sacramento Kings to provide veteran leadership as San Antonio's young guys developed. Still, they've eclipsed him in importance, which is problematic given his long, massive contract.

The Spurs likely won't resolve this for some time, as there will be few or no trade suitors.

articles.title: Blockbuster NBA Trade Idea To Shake Up the Eastern Conference
articles.summary: It's early (obviously), but the Eastern Conference looks as deep as ever.
articles.body:
It's early (obviously), but the Eastern Conference looks as deep as ever.

If any team hopes to escape it, they'll need to make any roster improvements they can between now and the Feb. 11 trade deadline.

In a nutshell, that's the driving force behind this blockbuster trade-machine masterpiece.

On one side, a perennially competitive Orlando Magic club keeps getting undone by a persistent shooting shortage. On the other, you have a Brooklyn Nets team that should know it doesn't have nearly enough to compete right now and will need more star power whenever it's time to strike.

Both clubs can scratch the other's itch, though this deal has an interesting twist. For reasons that will be explained here in a bit, you have the long-term rebuilder parting with multiple draft picks and the hopefully-win-now suitor giving up the best player in the exchange.

Does that sound at all confusing? Don't worry, we're deep-diving into why these two teams could come together on a major trade that could have the whole conference taking note.

Orlando Magic receive: Michael Porter Jr., 2027 first-round pick (via NYK), 2028 first-round pick (1-8 protected, via PHI), 2029 second-round pick (via GSW) and 2029 second-round pick (via MEM)

Remember how, before last season, Orlando felt so squeezed for spacing that it forked over four first-round picks and a first-round pick swap for the good-but-definitely-not-great Desmond Bane?

Well, nothing really changed. Or, at least, not in a transformative way.

The Magic still couldn't shoot (24th in made threes, 27th in three-point percentage), and their offense merely leveled up from awful ( 27th in efficiency in 2024-25) to below-average ( 18th ). And since their defense really regressed over that same stretch (from second to 13th ), their overall net gain was a meager 0.8 points per 100 possessions.

Their first-round ceiling didn't budge. That's why Jamahl Mosley no longer coaches this club, and it's also why Orlando could have serious questions about the long-term viability of the Franz Wagner-Paolo Banchero partnership.

This trade gives Orlando an out. And maybe solves those spacing issues. And it even helps replenish some of the lost draft capital.

The Magic need shooting, and Porter offers as much as anyone realistically connected to the trade market. For his career, the 6'10" sharpshooter has netted 2.6 triples a night and converted his long-range looks at a 39.8 percent clip.

He is the kind of shooting threat who demands constant attention from an opposing defense, which might be exactly what the Magic need to unlock this offense. Banchero badly needs more breathing room to make the most of his powerful downhill game. And Porter's comfort in an off-ball role would make it easier to find extra on-ball opportunities for Bane and Anthony Black.

If Magic fans still aren't fully convinced, it's probably because Wagner is a better player than Porter in a vacuum. But when the parts don't add up to more than a bunch of first-round defeats, it's time to rethink how the whole comes together. A more cohesive roster and a handful of draft picks sound too enticing to pass up.

Brooklyn's roster might be temporarily led by Porter and Julius Randle, but the most important players for the franchise are 20-year-old sophomore Egor Dëmin and 20-year-old rookie Mikel Brown Jr. The Nets should be exploring every opportunity to brighten their futures.

Often, that means stockpiling as many draft picks as possible, but Brooklyn has long-term assets to spare. Especially when these first-round picks—one from the defending champs, one from the league's newest superteam—are far from the finest in the franchise's collection.

The Nets are already holding a bunch of lottery tickets. What they need is more of a guaranteed winner this group can grow with. That label is infinitely easier to apply to Wagner (a 25-year-old signed through 2029-30 ) than it would be to Porter (a 28-year-old on an expiring deal).

Now, Wagner's pact is pricey, but a team with this many rookie-scale contracts on the payroll can easily stomach it.

Plus, that's why the trade price is reasonable. A 6'10", in-prime swingman with this type of two-way versatility almost never becomes available, and they command top dollar when they do. The Nets are capitalizing on a couple of buy-low factors in their favor, like Wagner's wonky fit with Banchero and the fact he missed nearly 50 games last season.

Wagner, already a near-star now, could look a lot better somewhere else. And that somewhere just might be Brooklyn, since the Nets would have three different playmakers—four as long as they hang onto Julius Randle (an obvious trade candidate if this deal went down)—who all have off-ball utility (Wagner as a slasher, Brown and Dëmin as shooters).

If the Nets ace enough of their developmental projects, this core could be pretty special in a few seasons. That could allow Brooklyn's rise to coincide with several current Eastern Conference heavyweights aging out of contention.

articles.title: 'Our Crap Stinks,' Mike Brown Reacts to Knicks' 0-3 Start as Jalen Brunson Takes Blame
articles.summary: New York Knicks coach Mike Brown believes three straight losses might be a humbling his team needs as it tries to defend its NBA championship.
articles.body:
New York Knicks coach Mike Brown believes three straight losses might be a humbling his team needs as it tries to defend its NBA championship.

"Games like this will tell us, our crap stinks. It does," Brown said after a 111-102 defeat to the Orlando Magic, per ESPN's Vincent Goodwill . "And we're the only ones who can do anything about it. There's no light switch we can just turn on and go and win the ballgame. Nobody's giving us anything, so we have to be better with the little things until we start shooting the ball."

Knicks star Jalen Brunson said the buck stops with him.

"Everything falls on my shoulders," he told reporters while referencing the offense. "I just got to be a better leader when it comes to that, when it comes to our guys are ready to go in the right spots. There's a lot of other little things, but it's organization on my part."

Brunson had a game-high 28 points against the Magic but shot just 1-of-7 from beyond the arc.

For the most part, the starting lineup delivered, though Mikal Bridges was held in check. One big difference was the bench as Magic reserves Tristan da Silva and Anthony Black combined to score 37 points. New York's bench, on the other hand, had 11 points collectively.

Brunson thinks the Knicks "get a little comfortable" when they have dominant stretches. Then the momentum dissipates.

"We have to continue to put our foot on the gas and execute things like we did last year," he said, per The Athletic's James L. Edwards III . "We're not going to be the same. We're not going to play how we were playing last year; that's just human nature. But we have to accept this part of the journey, find a way to get better, and hopefully after a couple of games, we can look back and say, 'We grew from that.'"

A consequence of winning the title is that a team will likely have a difficult first week. The NBA wants to leverage the excitement of a new season to maximum effect, and that means having high-profile matchups.

The Knicks have had to face off with three playoff teams from a year ago. They tipped off the campaign against the new-look Philadelphia 76ers before taking on the Boston Celtics and then Orlando.

An 0-3 record obviously isn't ideal, but it can be beneficial from the standpoint of getting everybody refocused.

Another Eastern Conference contender is on tap next, the Detroit Pistons. The Knicks host them Tuesday at Madison Square Garden.

Notching a victory would go some way toward lowering the anxiety level in the Big Apple.

articles.summary: Los Angeles Clippers veteran guard Kris Dunn is facing a wave of backlash following Oklahoma City Thunder forward Jalen Williams' devastating injury in Sunday's matchup, but one former player is coming to his defense.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Clippers veteran guard Kris Dunn is facing a wave of backlash following Oklahoma City Thunder forward Jalen Williams' devastating injury in Sunday's matchup, but one former player is coming to his defense.

Former NBA star Jim Jackson, who now works as a color commentator for the Clippers, pushed back against the narrative that Dunn purposefully intended to injure Williams.

"Kris Dunn is not a dirty player," Jackson said after the Clippers' 108-101 loss . "It's unfortunate that it has happened. We are sending prayers to him and his family and the organization."

Dunn appeared to shove Williams in the back as he went up for a dunk late in the fourth quarter, which caused him to land awkwardly and suffer a serious leg injury. He was stretchered off the court, and his teammates were visibly shaken in the aftermath.

"We're not doing great," Thunder head coach Mark Daigneault admitted after the game .

This is Dunn's 11th season in the NBA, and he's known as a hard-nosed defender who takes on the toughest assignment on a nightly basis. He will have some work to do to repair his reputation following Williams' injury.

The Clippers (1-2) will try to end their two-game skid when they meet the Los Angeles Lakers (3-0) on Wednesday.

articles.title: 'S--t We Got an MVP,' LeBron Reacts to Playing Center with Joel Embiid on 76ers' Roster
articles.summary: While he has served as a makeshift center at times for the Philadelphia 76ers, that's not a role LeBron James is looking to occupy on a regular basis this season.
articles.body:
While he has served as a makeshift center at times for the Philadelphia 76ers, that's not a role LeBron James is looking to occupy on a regular basis this season.

"Well, s--t, we got an MVP over there," he said in reference to Joel Embiid after Sunday's 106-93 loss to the Detroit Pistons, per ESPN's Kris Rhim . "I'm not here to have a sustainable role at the 5. You got Joel Embiid on the team. ... If I was to say I was signed here to have a sustainable role at the 5, I don't think none of us would actually want that. I can do it, but... we have [Embiid]."

Mostly through tactical necessity, James moved over to center for stretches in the season-opening win over the New York Knicks. Embiid, who was battling foul trouble, pitched the idea to the coaching staff mid-game.

Once again, coach Nick Nurse had little other choice but to deploy LeBron at the 5 on Sunday as the team rested Embiid on the second half of a back-to-back.

This will be an ongoing push and pull because Philly's center depth took a major blow with Ariel Hukporti's torn Achilles.

Even if he stays healthy all year, Embiid will miss games through load management, and he isn't going to play 40-plus minutes a night. When the seven-time All-Star isn't on the floor, using James as a small-ball center is probably the Sixers' most effective strategy. However, a 41-year-old LeBron will understandably have some reservations with that as he monitors his workload across the entire regular season.

Adem Bona had six points, 13 rebounds and three blocks in 25 minutes against Detroit. Perhaps he'll build on that and establish himself as a good backup big.

Even if that happens, the Sixers' center situation is going to be a subplot to follow throughout the campaign.

articles.title: Jalen Suggs Injured, Latest on Magic Star After Scary Knee Injury
articles.summary: The Orlando Magic are dealing with a major injury scare after starting point guard Jalen Suggs went down late in Sunday's 111-102 win over the New York Knicks.
articles.body:
The Orlando Magic are dealing with a major injury scare after starting point guard Jalen Suggs went down late in Sunday's 111-102 win over the New York Knicks.

Per ESPN's Vincent Goodwill , Suggs suffered "an apparent noncontact right knee injury" and had to be helped off the court with 2:09 remaining in the fourth quarter. Magic head coach Sean Sweeney reportedly "did not have an update on Suggs after the game... beyond saying that he will be evaluated."

Suggs was on a breakaway fast break and attempted to go up for a layup when his right knee appeared to buckle. He remained on the floor in pain for several minutes before being helped to his feet and walking gingerly to the locker room with assistance from team personnel.

Sweeney added that he talked briefly with Suggs after the game, and the 25-year-old was in good spirits.

Suggs has been limited to just 92 games combined over the last two seasons due to various injuries. His latest setback comes after Orlando lost star forward Paolo Banchero to a low-grade high ankle sprain that is expected to keep him sidelined for multiple weeks.

If Suggs is forced to miss time, Anthony Black will likely take over as the Magic's starting point guard. The 22-year-old had 18 points and five assists in his season debut on Sunday.

The Magic (1-2) will continue their road trip with a matchup against the Toronto Raptors (2-1) on Wednesday.

articles.title: Jaylen Brown-Jayson Tatum Drama Addressed by Celtics HC Joe Mazzulla
articles.summary: Boston Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla remained diplomatic as some of the past tension between Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum appears to be rising to the surface.
articles.body:
Boston Celtics coach Joe Mazzulla remained diplomatic as some of the past tension between Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum appears to be rising to the surface.

"Those two guys, they were together for (nine seasons), and they had great, great moments together," Mazzulla said, per The Athletic's Jay King . "And at the end of the day, nobody is perfect. We all can be better. We all did great things. We all did things that we want to be better at. So, I think it's more just focusing on the greatness that those two were able to achieve and the fact that they're both great people."

The coach went on to say Tatum and Brown are "different," both in terms of their playing styles and personalities.

"It doesn't mean that it's good or bad. They're just different," he said. "So, you focus on the high character. We're focused on Jayson because he's with us; he plays for us, he's our guy. We're grateful for what Jaylen did in the past, but our focus goes to Jayson — who he is as a player, who he is as a person — and then we just move on from there."

From the moment the Celtics traded Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers, there was a general belief the move reflected a need to break up he and Tatum. The pair weren't openly feuding, but the partnership had run its course after nine years.

Now that they're on rival teams, the facade might be crumbling a bit.

Brown implied Tatum wasn't being entirely truthful when he said he was as surprised as everyone else to learn his longtime running mate was on the way out.

The five-time All-Star went a step further when he claimed "there's no beef" with Tatum before hinting at an underlying frustration.

"Jayson's a great guy," Brown told reporters . "Like I said, great family, hell of a basketball player, hell of a PR team. There's no beef, but it'll be a little lamb chop."

More than anything, this is all underlining why the Brown trade needed to happen. It doesn't take much reading between the lines to see there was likely some lingering unease inside Boston's locker room last season.

If Brown remained on the Celtics, managing the relationship with he and Tatum would've been a delicate balancing act for Mazzulla and his staff all year.

Gripes are hard to find amid the Los Angeles Lakers' 3-0 start to the 2026-27 NBA season.

For everything going the way of the Purple and Gold so far—undefeated, in possession of the Association's fourth-best net rating , per NBA.com—there is a clear weak spot with this roster that, if not addressed, could become a bigger issue down the line.

Blockbuster Trade Idea To Shake Up the East

The Lakers need to upgrade their backup center spot over incumbent Kevon Looney. And they seemingly know it, as they reportedly tried to land bouncy backup Jericho Sims from the Milwaukee Bucks before the season, but "those discussions were derailed by Milwaukee's intent to extract two future second-round picks in the deal and the Lakers' insistence that they part with only one," per NBA insider Jake Fischer .

Now, that's not to suggest that L.A. was at all wrong about its valuation of Sims or the assets that would've been required to land him. He has made all of one appearance (spanning just two minutes) over Milwaukee's first three games.

A single second-round pick was a reasonable walk-away price point for L.A.

What this highlights, rather, is the need to address this position at some point. And with the Lakers perhaps positioning themselves for a deep playoff run, they would presumably want to land this upgrade sooner than later to offer ample time to incorporate the new player into their plans.

Because Sims, of course, is just one of many players capable of filling this void.

Lakers' insider Jovan Buha , for instance, argued for a reunion with Los Angeles Clippers center Brook Lopez, a member of the 2017-18 Lakers. The skilled 7-footer is off to a strong start this season, threatening to spoil that unblemished record with a 22-point, three-block effort when these clubs collided on Friday night.

"[Lopez] is just better than Looney," Buha opined," Looney is probably a better screener and rebounder, Lopez is better at just about everything else ... and he might just be one of the most attainable backup bigs."

With the Clippers having abandoned all hopes of contending after the summer subtraction of Kawhi Leonard, they wouldn't figure to cling too tightly onto a 38-year-old reserve. Especially since they have a deep draft pick deficit to work their way out of now.

Could the Lakers have better luck in talks with the Clippers than they did with the Bucks? Maybe. If nothing else, it's certainly worth a phone to call find out.

As with Sims, though, this search doesn't need to end with Lopez. It just has to deliver someone. Walker Kessler deserves some credit for this, but it also speaks to the lack of reliable options behind him that L.A. has fared a whopping 28.8 points worse per 100 possessions without Kessler on the floor.

The Lakers clearly can't afford that kind of slippage. And they'd be in serious trouble if Kessler, who missed all but five games last season due to left shoulder sugery, were forced to miss any time.

If L.A. wants to keep the good times rolling, it has to guard itself the times that won't be so good. Upgrading the backup center spot should be a simple, cost-effective way of working toward that goal.

articles.title: 3 NBA teams that should already be worried
articles.summary: Should these NBA teams hit the panic button?
articles.body:
The NBA season has just started, and some fan bases could be close to hitting the panic button. Some teams have started the season with low expectations.

The Sacramento Kings and Brooklyn Nets are 0-3, but those fans knew what they were getting into. Some franchises came in with championship aspirations, but now they're wondering if this could be a nightmare season.

It's really early in the season, and teams could still be shaking off the rust. Teams like the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs are coming off long playoff runs, so they might need some extra time.

Here are three teams that should be worried already.

The New York Knicks are 0-3, and the vibes are just bad. They played two of the better teams in the Eastern Conference but lost to an Orlando Magic team without Paolo Banchero . It doesn't help that three of their main players want contract extensions but haven't gotten them yet.

Karl-Anthony Towns, Josh Hart, and Miles McBride have all been vocal about seeking new deals. It's not an ideal start to the year for a team that just won a championship. Trades probably haven't happened yet, but you never know what James Dolan will do. They are the first defending champions to go 0-3 since the 2011-2012 Dallas Mavericks .

The Golden State Warriors could face a long, dreadful season. They're winless, have an aging roster, and one of their free agent signings might never play basketball again. Kristaps Porziņģis is out indefinitely due to symptoms of POTS (Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome).

They blew a 12-point lead to the Memphis Grizzlies and just looked like a team that didn't trust each other. Jimmy Butler will return from an ACL injury, but he probably won't be enough to save this team. The lone bright spot for this squad is that Stephen Curry signed a two-year contract extension before the season started.

Giannis Antetokounmpo was traded to the Miami Heat in one of the biggest NBA offseason moves. It hasn't worked out so far, as the Heat haven't collected a win yet. Their offense has looked clunky, and their defense has been horrendous. They've given up at least 115 points in all three losses this season.

They have some time to figure out how Giannis and Bam Adebayo will work together. They clearly haven't found the formula yet. Heat head coach Erik Spoelstra is one of the best coaches in the NBA, so Miami fans should have faith that he'll figure this out.

articles.title: NBA strikes deals with Kalshi and Polymarket, with eye on integrity and regulations
articles.summary: The NBA has struck deals that will make Kalshi and Polymarket the league’s preferred prediction markets, along with an agreement with a federal agency tasked with regulating those exchanges.
articles.body: MIAMI — The NBA has struck deals that will make Kalshi and Polymarket the league’s preferred prediction markets, along with an agreement with a federal agency tasked with regulating those exchanges. Those agreements, announced Monday, are intended to provide “significant integrity protections for NBA-related markets,” including limitations on what can be offered on those exchanges, transparency when it comes to suspicious patterns by site users, and banning league and team personnel from making trades related to league events. The prediction markets will have “information-sharing obligations relating to investigations and suspicious trading,” the NBA said. The NBA has had similar guardrails in place with its sportsbook partners for some time and has cited instances where that system has flagged irregularities in betting patterns. “If you’re going to be betting on our games or trading on our games or playing fantasy around our games, it’s better for it to be regulated than unregulated,” said Scott Kaufman-Ross, the NBA’s head of media distribution and partnerships. “And clearly, our fans have interest in this activity. So, we’re in a better position to protect the integrity of our games in a regulated market where there’s transparency, where things can be monitored and we have insight into what’s happening.” The NBA is also expanding its agreements with current official sports betting partners, such as DraftKings, to include their prediction-market offerings. Not all states offer legalized sports betting, but prediction markets — at least on some level — are essentially available in all 50 states. More than a dozen states are involved in litigation over prediction markets and earlier this month the NFL asked the Supreme Court to rule on the regulation of such markets. The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission contends that it has exclusive jurisdiction on oversight, though some states believe it should fall under their purview. Earlier this month, the NBA told sportsbooks they will not be permitted to offer certain types of wagering this season, including but not limited to which players record the first stat of a game, the outcome of the opening tip and taking the “under” involving players not expected to play more than a few minutes. The deals announced on Monday are expected to have similar restraints. “A big part of this is a limitation on the types of markets that can be offered,” Kaufman-Ross said. “We will have the right to approve the types of markets that are available on our games, which is a very important component for us. And we’ve had very constructive dialogues with the companies as part of that.” The NBA’s memorandum of understanding with the CFTC “reflects a shared commitment to ensuring that NBA-related prediction markets are subject to appropriate regulatory oversight and integrity protections,” the league said. Kalshi and Polymarket, as part of their partnerships with the NBA, will now be able to describe themselves as the “Preferred Prediction Market Exchange of the NBA,” plus have access to league intellectual property such as logos, be able to get NBA statistical data from league partner Sportradar “to operate and settle authorized NBA-related markets,” and other marketing activations. The terms of the NBA’s agreements with Kalshi and Polymarket were not disclosed, other than the league confirming that they are for multiple years. There are NBA stars with business relationships with those markets; Miami’s Giannis Antetokounmpo has promoted Kalshi and Philadelphia’s LeBron James recently signed a deal with Polymarket. At least one other NBA star, San Antonio’s Victor Wembanyama, recently said he will never endorse such sites.

This is all a consequence of the Dream's regular home venue, Gateway Center Arena, seating only 3,500 fans. The Dream and the WNBA would be leaving a lot of money on the table by having playoff games there instead of much larger State Farm Arena.

However, the start of the NBA season has collided with the WNBA postseason, presenting logistical hurdles to utilizing the Hawks' regular home arena. Game 4 of the Finals ended just hours before the Hawks' home opener, which was pushed back by 30 minutes from its original start time.

In the meantime, the WNBA is potentially looking at a championship-clinching game wrapping up on a Thursday afternoon. That's not ideal for players, fans or media partners.

It almost harkens back to a time when the NBA aired its Finals games on tape delay .

articles.title: WNBA Finals: League to hold Game 6 Thursday at State Farm Arena
articles.summary: The Dream have played all their home playoff games at State Farm Arena this postseason.
articles.body:
After days of deliberation, the WNBA has finally determined where and when Game 6 of the Finals will be played. The league announced Monday the contest will be held at 12:30 p.m. ET Thursday at State Farm Arena.

The decision comes after it was reported Sunday the league was unclear about both the time and place in which the game would be played, and was working with the Atlanta Dream, Golden State Valkyries, NBA and the Atlanta Hawks to come up with a solution.

In order to accommodate Thursday's game, the league opted to move it to earlier in the day. That decision allows both the Dream and Hawks to play home games at State Farm Arena on Thursday.

In a statement, WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert said the league saw the success of Games 3 and 4 and wanted to host Game 6 in the same arena.

"The sellout crowds and extraordinary atmosphere at State Farm Arena for Games 3 and 4 were a tremendous success, and we're excited to give thousands more fans the opportunity to experience Game 6 with a championship on the line," said WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert. "We thank the NBA, Dream, Valkyries, Hawks, State Farm Arena and USA Network for the collaboration and flexibility that made this move possible. We look forward to delivering another unforgettable Finals experience in Atlanta."

The WNBA knew Saturday — when the Valkyries evened the series with a 67-62 win in Game 4 — that scheduling Game 6 was going to take some work. Throughout the playoffs, the Dream have played home games at State Farm Arena — where the Hawks play their home games. That decision was partially due to fan demand, as the Dream's current home stadium, Gateway Center Arena, has the smallest capacity in the league, with just 3,500 seats. State Farm Arena can hold 17,000 fans.

But Game 6 provided the WNBA with a major scheduling conflict, as the Hawks were scheduled to play the Cleveland Cavaliers at State Farm Arena on the same day and at roughly the same time as the WNBA planned to hold Game 6 of the Finals.

The Hawks and Cavaliers were initially scheduled to play at 7 p.m. ET on Thursday. The Dream and Valkyries were initially scheduled to play at 8 p.m. ET on Thursday. With the change the Hawks and Cavaliers will now tip off at 8 p.m. ET.

When asked whether the early tip time would impact the game, Dream guard Allisha Gray said it didn't matter when the two teams played.

"I mean, it's the Finals. You just gotta do what you gotta do. We're locked in on winning Game 6. I don't care if we're playing at 8 a.m., 10 a.m., midnight. We've got a championship to win."

Dream coach Karl Smesko agreed, saying shootaround might be affected, but that's it.

It wasn't the first time in the series the league had to change its scheduling. In order to work around the Hawks' schedule, the WNBA moved Game 3 of the Finals up a day and adjusted the time of Game 4 so both contests could be held at State Farm Arena. It was a successful move, as the Dream sold out both games at the stadium.

On Sunday, it was reported that similar options were on the table for Game 6, including the WNBA moving back the date of the contest by a day to accommodate both teams. That solution came with a catch, however, as it would require the league to also shift the date of a possible Game 7 to ensure both teams received adequate rest before taking the court for the game. Ultimately, the league found another solution.

With the Game 6 situation finally sorted out, the WNBA shouldn't have to worry about the issue again. The Dream will begin playing their home games at State Farm Arena in 2027.

articles.title: 'We're not doing great': What Jalen Williams' injury could mean for Thunder
articles.summary: OKC's second-best player suffered a gruesome left leg injury on Sunday night.
articles.body:
You didn't need to physically be at Paycom Center to understand the severity of Thunder wing Jalen Williams' gruesome left leg injury suffered on Sunday night — you could hear and see everything.

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, unable to even look in Williams' direction as he lay under the basket, covering his face in his jersey, trying to gather himself.

The in-game announcers, whose literal job it is to entertain and communicate, struggling to find the right words.

The fans, attempting to process what had just happened in real time, visibly shaken, either turning away or covering their mouths with their hands.

And then there was Williams himself, who was consumed by so much shock he couldn't utter a scream or shout, looking down in disbelief at his leg in a position it was certainly not supposed to be in, before trainers could whisk him away on a stretcher.

"We're not doing great," head coach Mark Daigneault said following the 108-101 win . "That's tough on the guys. We're planning on coming in tomorrow, and I'm holding that because I think it's good to get around each other when you go through some tough situations. We'll come in, we'll regroup tomorrow, and see where we're at."

Injuries are sports' worst enemy, not just because of their cruelty, but because of their unpredictable cadence. (As of Monday afternoon, the full extent of Williams' injury is unknown.) Spend some time around this team, and you'll quickly understand not only how close-knit that Thunder locker room is, but how deeply they were affected by Williams' absence last season. The 25-year-old was limited to just 33 games dealing with hamstring and wrist injuries, a void that necessitated others filling in, and an unfortunate reminder of the costs of contention.

In the games that Williams missed, reserve 3&D guard Cason Wallace was the most commonly used deputy. While there isn't anyone on the roster truly capable of replicating Williams' blend of high-usage playmaking, shot creation and switchable point-of-attack defense, Wallace offers a similar stopper skill set and more consistent shooting.

But Wallace wasn't designated to be Williams' backup this season; he was inserted into the starting lineup alongside Williams due to the offseason departure of Lu Dort. With Williams sidelined, perhaps the Thunder will turn to Ajay Mitchell. Over 114 possessions last season — a relatively small sample size — the SGA/Mitchell/Wallace/Chet Holmgren/Isaiah Hartenstein pairing was a whopping plus-31.5 with a 99th percentile effective field goal percentage. This same group has played just six possessions this season, albeit with a similar plus-33.3 net rating.

Alternatively, Daigneault could roll with one of Alex Caruso or Jared McCain, each option bringing different things to the table. Caruso is a low-volume creator, similar to Wallace, but offers immense veteran savvy and poise. McCain is a volume shooter whose recent uptick in confidence and efficiency could offer the scoring punch lost with Williams. Oklahoma City trotted out 31 different starting lineups last year over the 82-game regular season, which is indicative of bad luck with injuries but also speaks to the sheer depth on the roster, with Daigneault able to experiment with a myriad of groups.

The natural answer, however, is the sliding scale shifting back toward Gilgeous-Alexander's end. The reigning MVP had quietly taken on more of an off-ball role this season than he was accustomed to in efforts to lessen his workload (and likely prevent any injuries), but his efficiency has cratered to levels not seen since his rookie campaign and his gravity hasn't yet translated into ball movement. (The Thunder are 27th in assists , unseen territory for a championship group.) One of the many benefits to having a healthy Williams was the ability to trot him out as a lead creator alongside the second unit while keeping the ship steady. Oklahoma City was a plus-229 in nearly 2,000 possessions with Williams on the floor last season — keeping that level of production up this time around will be more taxing on a thinner group.

There is also the possibility, perhaps down the line, of a trade. It's no secret that the Thunder's offensive struggles — 23rd in offensive rating at the time of this writing — are a bit more than early-season rust and, considering the different makeup of this team, it might make sense to get aggressive on the market earlier rather than later.

As for what a prolonged absence could mean for their title chances, I still have the Thunder among the top-2 with the San Antonio Spurs in the Western Conference (although the likes of Houston and Minnesota are making some of these assumptions increasingly difficult). The initial shock of Williams' prognosis will take time for the team to accept and adjust, but over time a leveling out will prevail. This isn't the first time they've been forced to deal without their second-best player — but to this degree, and under these new circumstances, the Thunder's immediate and future timeline could be affected.

articles.body:
Notre Dame announced Monday that Fighting Irish legend Skylar Diggins will work as a special advisor to head coach Niele Ivey.

Ivey said the seven-time WNBA All-Star "will help elevate our program through her leadership, expertise and unique perspective as both a former student-athlete and accomplished professional":

"Skylar's loyalty and commitment to the University have been unmatched. Her ability to motivate, elevate, and inspire our student-athletes will strengthen our culture, enhance our team, and create meaningful opportunities for growth and development.

"Her impact will extend far beyond the game, helping shape the next generation of student-athletes and continuing to build a legacy of excellence within our program. Welcome home, Skylar!"

Diggins had a decorated career during her four-year run in South Bend. She averaged 15.7 points and 5.0 assists in 150 appearances. She was a first-team All-American in 2011-12 and 2012-13, and she left as Notre Dame's all-time leading scorer (2,357 points). Arike Ogunbowale and Hannah Hidalgo have since surpassed her.

Diggins was also a driving force behind the Fighting Irish finishing as national runners-up in the 2011 and 2012 NCAA tournaments. They reached the Final Four again in her senior year.

Between that and the success she has enjoyed in the WNBA, the 36-year-old guard is a great representative for Notre Dame basketball.

This is part of a larger trend as schools are using distinguished alumni to help attract talent in a recruiting landscape made more competitive by NIL and the transfer portal.

For Diggins, this might be a way to get some formal experience if she hopes to transition to coaching once her WNBA career concludes.

articles.title: New Jaylen Brown Rumors Update Buzz on Jayson Tatum Relationship Before Celtics-76ers Trade
articles.summary: Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum may not have any beef after the former was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers on Sunday, but the Boston Celtics may have helped cook up the "lamb chops and some gravy" between the two men that Brown referenced when asked about his relationship with Tatum.
articles.body:
Jaylen Brown and Jayson Tatum may not have any beef after the former was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers on Sunday, but the Boston Celtics may have helped cook up the "lamb chops and some gravy" between the two men that Brown referenced when asked about his relationship with Tatum.

"I had heard the Sixers thing was sitting on the table for a while as a possibility. It seemed unlikely, but it was sitting there. And I think kind of hiding in the weeds a little bit through all this is the Celtics. Because I feel like they're the ones, the main ones that created this," ESPN's Marc Spears said during Monday's NBA Today. "They favored Jayson. Jayson didn't ask them to favor him. Jayson didn't stop it, but they favored Jayson. And I know Jaylen felt some type of way about that. And Jaylen also was in the community, won a lot of people over, was very vocal. I'm not gonna say he was a saint and everything as well. But at some point these guys hopefully will talk. I just think it's too hot right now. The trade isn't too far away, but the Celtics definitely deserve some of this blame."

The relationship between Brown and Tatum has been a popular topic of conversation following this summer's surprising trade between the Sixers and Celtics, and Tatum reinvigorated it recently when he said in a video that he was "just as much caught off guard as the rest of the world" by the deal.

Brown wasn't buying it, hitting Tatum with the cap emoji under the video.

Brown was then asked by reporters if there was beef between Tatum and himself.

"We both got so much stuff in front of us," he told reporters. "So at the end of the day... he gotta do what he's got to do for his team. I gotta do what I do for my team. Jayson's a great guy. Like I said, great family, hell of a basketball player, hell of a PR team. There's no beef, but it'll be a little lamb chop."

He added that Tatum "should stay ready at all times."

"There's no beef. It's not about that. It should be more praise," he told reporters Friday. "I understand drama gets clicks and views, but I'm not really into that. I'm not blaming everybody for how they feel. Everybody is entitled to their own feelings, and we all go through different things in our lives."

In case you were wondering, the Sixers and Celtics play for the first time this season on Nov. 10. Consider it appointment viewing for NBA fans.

articles.title: WNBA championship may be decided on a Thursday morning because an NBA game took priority
articles.summary: The WNBA scheduled its potential championship-clinching game between the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream for 12:30 p.m. ET on Thursday.
articles.body: The WNBA scheduled its potential championship-clinching game for 12:30 p.m. ET on Thursday, the league announced, settling a logistical nightmare that appeared to have few satisfactory solutions. The Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream’s Game 6 had always been set for Thursday night in Georgia with its location and exact tipoff time listed as TBD due to an unfortunate series of scheduling conflicts. The Dream’s playoff home, State Farm Arena, has an Atlanta Hawks game scheduled for Thursday night. “We thank the NBA, Dream, Valkyries, Hawks, State Farm Arena and USA Network for the collaboration and flexibility that made this move possible,” retiring WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert said in a statement on Monday afternoon. The Dream played most of its 2026 season at the 3,500-seat Gateway Center Arena at College Park, the league’s smallest building. But the team had been able to move major regular seasons games and all playoff contests to State Farm Arena, the 17,000-seat home of the NBA’s Atlanta Hawks. But with Game 6 set for Thursday, the same day as a 7 p.m. Cleveland Cavaliers-Hawks game at State Farm, that big venue was not available for a prime time women’s game. If the Valkyries win Monday’s Game 5 in San Francisco, that means their West Coast fans would have to get to a TV by 9:30 a.m. PT on Thursday and possibly pop champagne bottles before noon should Golden State wrap it up in Atlanta. In the WNBA’s prepared statement, Engellbert did not address the odd start time, but instead chose to focus on the league playing in front a larger crowd. “The sellout crowds and extraordinary atmosphere of State Farm Arena for Games 3 and 4 were a tremendous success and we’re excited to give thousands more fans the opportunity to experience Game 6 with a championship on the line,” Engellbert said.

articles.title: Auburn basketball signee Mantas Rubstavicius dismisses lawsuit against NCAA
articles.summary: Auburn basketball signee Mantas Rubstavicius voluntarily dismissed his lawsuit against NCAA and subsequent fight for college eligibility Monday.
articles.body:
AUBURN — Mantas Rubstavicius , the Auburn basketball signee who sued the NCAA earlier this month in pursuit of eligibility for the upcoming season, dismissed his lawsuit Monday, Oct. 26, according to court documents obtained by the Montgomery Advertiser.

At 3:22 p.m. CT Monday, attorneys representing Rubstavicius and the NCAA filed a "Joint Stipulation of Dismissal with Prejudice," with presiding Judge Jeffrey Tickal granting the dismissal two minutes later.

Auburn told the Montgomery Advertiser it had been informed Rubstavicius voluntarily dismissed, providing the following statement from head coach Steven Pearl: "Mantas is an exceptional young man with a bright future ahead of him. We appreciate the time he spent as part of our Auburn basketball family and wish him nothing but success as he takes this next step in his career. We look forward to following his success both on and off the court."

Rubstavicius' legal action sought "judgement, declaratory relief and an order enjoining the NCAA from denying him the opportunity" to participate in the upcoming, as Auburn had two requests and a final appeal for Rubstavicius' eligibility denied last month. He signed "binding" revenue-sharing and financial aid agreements with Auburn weeks before the NCAA unveiled new eligibility requirements to member schools on May 8, with court documents listing those respective agreements as signed April 25 and May 3.

The 24-year-old Lithuanian had a lengthy professional career overseas, playing in two leagues for four different squads since 2018. He also went through the 2024 NBA draft process but wasn't selected, though he played for the Golden State Warriors summer league team.

Adam Cole is the Auburn athletics beat writer for the Montgomery Advertiser. He can be reached via email at acole@gannett.com or on X, the platform formerly known as Twitter, @colereporter . To support Adam's work, please subscribe to the Montgomery Advertiser .

articles.title: Bucks vs. Pacers, will a new chapter be added to the rivalry tonight?
articles.summary: Indiana Pacers star and Oshkosh native Tyrese Haliburton is back. Will a new chapter to the Bucks-Pacers rivalry be added on Oct. 26?
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Bucks are looking for their first win of the season and the first for Taylor Jenkins as the team's head coach when they host the Indiana Pacers tonight at Fiserv Forum. The Bucks have lost three straight to begin the season, which is the first time that has happened since 2015-16.

Indiana is coming off a victory over Brooklyn on Oct. 25 and is 2-1.

Will the Bucks vs. Pacers rivalry add a new chapter?

Milwaukee vs. Indiana had become one of the league's spiciest rivalries since the 2023-24 season, when Oshkosh native and Pacers star Tyrese Haliburton used the "Dame Time" celebration late in a Pacers' NBA Cup victory over Damian Lillard and the Bucks. That rivalry got even more heated, with flagrant fouls, ejections, postgame melees, intense playoff matchups, taunts, inappropriate fan interactions and public address announcers mispronouncing player names.

The Bucks added some fuel to the matchup last season when they signed Myles Turner away from the Pacers, and then Giannis Antetokounmpo hit a buzzer-beater in Turner's homecoming Nov. 3 that may or may not have included an incendiary celebration of his own. The Pacers were also the last team Antetokounmpo played against as a member of the Bucks on March 15.

The rivalry between the organizations has even translated to the baseball diamond, when Haliburton said the Milwaukee Brewers rescinded an offer to throw out a ceremonial pitch in 2025.

Then, before a Sept. 3 game between the Brewers and Chicago Cubs, the North Siders had Haliburton throw out the ceremonial first pitch at Wrigley Field.

First-year Bucks guard Kasparas Jakučionis was fined twice by the NBA for flopping, as the league reviewed two plays involving the 20-year-old on Oct. 23 vs. Chicago and Oct. 24 vs. Philadelphia.

Jakučionis was assessed a $2,000 fine for each incident.

articles.title: Devin Vassell exhorts Spurs to 'become the hunters again'
articles.summary: The seventh-year guard called on himself and his teammates to ramp up their intensity level beginning with Tuesday night's game against winless Sacramento.
articles.body:
Devin Vassell has plenty of reasons to cherish the Spurs' stunning run to the NBA Finals last season.

He hit timely shots. Blocked 7-footers at the rim. Provided poise and leadership.

But the seventh-year pro knows it's best to put it all behind him.

"We did what we did last year," he said. "That's gone and out the window."

Speaking to reporters after practice Monday, Vassell stressed the need for him and his teammate to stop resting on their laurels and ramp up their intensity level in a big way beginning with Tuesday night's home game against the winless Sacramento Kings.

Vassell took himself and his teammates to task after the defending Western Conference champions finished the first week of the season 1-2, a showing he said wasn't befitting of a team with championship aspirations.

"Honestly, we have a goal we want to reach and we're far away from that goal," Vassell said. "So we can't sit here and, I don't even know how to say it, jog our way through the season. No, we have to be honest from day one. And I feel like our first two games (losses to West powers Oklahoma City and Houston), we realized we can't just walk into a game and feel like we're just going to win a game because we're San Antonio."

The young Spurs shocked the league last season by winning 62 games before fearlessly fighting their way to the NBA Finals, where they lost in five games to the New York Knicks.

They should be proud of all of that, Vassell said. But they also need to put it out of their minds.

"We got to become the hunters again," he said. "I think we're a little bit drunk off the success of last year, and we have a lot of room to grow. So trying to just put that behind us because we're a new team. This is a new season."

Vassell said the Spurs giving up 30-plus points in the first quarter of each of their games underscores their lack of intensity. To solve their early game problems on the defensive end, he said they need to get back to "throwing the first punch, being more physical, not letting teams get to their spots, pushing them off their spots."

"I just think we're not playing to our standard," Julian Champagnie said. "We're not coming out with the level of intensity we need to. And obviously I think we've seen that against OKC, Houston. Obviously we got the 'W' in Dallas, but I think we still came out pretty lax in Dallas."

Champagnie said it all boils down to having the right mindset.

"We have the same players from last year," he said. "I don't think it's schematic. Everybody on the court can guard. The starting lineup can guard. The second unit can guard. We did it last year, so there's really no excuse for us not to do it this year."

Coach Mitch Johnson lit into the Spurs after they gave up 31 points in the first quarter against a Mavericks team playing without stars Cooper Flagg (shoulder) and Kyrie Irving (rest) and others. The Spurs went on to claim a 122-106 victory , but that didn't stop Johnson from giving his players an earful.

"We've played three games, and we've got stretches of the games where we're getting our butts kicked," Johnson said after the game. "There's a lot of things we can control and we've got to be better at that."

Champagnie said it's up to the players, not the coaches, to make that happen.

"In all instances, we have to hold each other accountable," he said. "Coach isn't on the floor. None of the coaches are on the floor. They always say that to us. We all have to go out there and be able to have those tough conversations with whoever it is."

Many of those "tough conversations" have already happened, Champagnie said.

"As players we always talk," he said. "I'm not going to go out here and tell you guys what we're talking about in the locker room, but we've had our own conversations and we know what we have to figure out."

"We got to sit here and beat teams," Vassell said. "We've got to impose our will, and we got to start doing that from today."
