articles.title: Jalen Williams Will Have Surgery After Gruesome Injury, Update on Thunder Star's Timeline to Return
articles.summary: The Oklahoma City Thunder will be without star Jalen Williams for the foreseeable future.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder will be without star Jalen Williams for the foreseeable future.

General manager Sam Presti told reporters Monday he suffered a fractured fibula and dislocated left ankle during Sunday's win over the Los Angeles Clippers. Presti explained Williams will need surgery and the exact timeline for his return will be known following the operation.

Williams suffered the gruesome injury with fewer than two minutes remaining in Sunday's game when he went up for an attempt at the rim and collided with Kris Dunn. He suffered the injury when he fell awkwardly and was stretchered off the court.

The Thunder crowd chanted his name as he was stretchered away.

Teammate Shai Gilgeous-Alexander was emotional after the game and said during an interview, "I don't even know. I just feel bad for him. Nothing more than that. ... It's obviously gonna be tough without a player like that. But he's not gone forever, he'll be back better than ever and we know it. We've just gotta hold the fort down until he comes back."

Williams' setback was all the more notable because he dealt with injury concerns throughout the 2025-26 campaign.

He appeared in just 33 regular-season games because of wrist and hamstring injuries and then played just five of OKC's playoff games. His absence was a significant factor in the team's loss to the San Antonio Spurs in the Western Conference Finals.

Unfortunately for the Thunder, Williams isn't the only injury situation they are dealing with early in the season.

Presti said Cason Wallace suffered a left labral tear in his shoulder and will also require surgery with an exact timeline to be determined.

"I like to say, and we say within our walls all the time," Presti continued . "There's a difference between being positive and being optimistic. Not going to sit up here and say this is exactly where we want to be or this is how we'd like to have it, but at the same time, we're extremely optimistic about the recovery for both players. Most importantly, things could've been a lot worse."

The Thunder reached the Western Conference Finals last season even with Williams dealing with injuries, but they will be missing two significant pieces of their roster for the foreseeable future following these setbacks.

articles.title: Dos horribles lesiones ponen la temporada de los Thunder cuesta arriba
articles.standfirst: Jalen Williams (tobillo izquierdo dislocado y fractura de peroné) y Cason Wallace (desgarro del labrum en su hombro izquierdo) serán operados y estarán de baja indefinidamente
articles.summary: Jalen Williams (tobillo izquierdo dislocado y fractura de peroné) y Cason Wallace (desgarro del labrum en su hombro izquierdo) serán operados y estarán de baja indefinidamente
articles.body: Después de tres encuentros, la temporada de los Thunder se tambalea. No por los resultados, pues han ganado los tres, sino por las terribles lesiones sufridas por Jalen Williams y Cason Wallace frente a los Clippers. Los dos titulares tendrán que pasar por el quirófano y estarán de baja durante un tiempo sin determinar. El primero es probable que se pierda toda la campaña. El segundo, con un poco de suerte, podría estar para el tramo final. Las pruebas a las que han sido sometidos ambos jugadores han arrojado diagnósticos que no por esperados dejan de ser demoledores. Wiliams sufre una dislocación del tobillo izquierdo y una fractura de peroné. El alero se lesionó al hacer una entrada a canasta cuando faltaba poco más de un minuto para el final del partido. Fue desequilibrado en el aire y cayó de malísima manera. Su pie fuera de lugar alarmó a compañeros, rivales y a todo el banquillo de los Thunder, de donde salieron a toda prisa los miembros del cuerpo médico. Cason Wallace, mientras, sufrió un desgarro de lábrum en su hombro izquierdo después de chocar con Isaiah Jackson en un bloqueo. Corría el minuto seis de partido. Tras el golpe, se quedó unos instantes tendido en el suelo con evidentes gestos de dolor y también tuvo que ser atendido. Después se marchó al vestuario y no volvió a salir. Los Thunder, en una jornada aciaga, se quedaban sin dos piezas básicas y sus aspiraciones de anillo, de repente, se ven drásticamente reducidas salvo que hagan algún movimiento en la plantilla. Y quizás ni así. "Los recuperaremos, los pondremos en forma, pero aún nos queda mucho baloncesto por jugar. Tenemos que organizarnos, averiguar cuáles son los próximos pasos porque esto es parte del negocio en el que estamos", anticipó el mánager general de la franquicia, Sam Presti. Tampoco ha tenido mucho tiempo de pensar en operaciones de mercado. "Para mí, las últimas 24 horas o sin importar cuánto tiempo haya pasado, todo ha sido sobre las personas. En este tipo de situaciones, es importante hacer balance, dar un paso atrás y darnos cuenta de que estamos tratando con personas", confesó antes de alabar la actitud de sus jugadores: "Ves lo duro que trabajan. Cuánto les importa. Creo que este equipo me ha enseñado mucho. La forma en que están tan conectados y la forma en que se preocupan el uno por el otro. Es inspirador".

articles.title: Ole Miss Basketball Resolves Tampering Case with No Further NCAA Penalties
articles.summary: OXFORD, Miss. (AP) — The NCAA has decided against penalizing Mississippi basketball coach Chris Beard, meaning his program faces no further penalties related to an infractions case involving a former assistant coach who committed tampering violations.
articles.body:
OXFORD, Miss. (AP) — The NCAA has decided against penalizing Mississippi basketball coach Chris Beard, meaning his program faces no further penalties related to an infractions case involving a former assistant coach who committed tampering violations.

Beard "was not personally involved in the violations, was not aware of the impermissible contact and promoted an atmosphere for compliance," the NCAA announced in a statement Friday. "Thus, the parties agreed that he should not receive any penalties."

The NCAA found that former assistant Wes Flanigan had "impermissible recruiting conversations with the advisor of a student-athlete from another school who had not entered the transfer portal."

The player, who was not identified, subsequently entered the portal but never visited Ole Miss and wound up at another school.

The NCAA has accepted penalties that Ole Miss had already agreed to serve in connection with the case during the past two seasons, including two years of probation, a $455,000 fine, a one-week ban on all recruiting communications for the men's basketball program and a one-week prohibition on prospective player visits.

Ole Miss said in a statement the university was pleased to have resolved the matter with "no ongoing or future impact on our basketball program ... or any other athletics program."

Meanwhile, the NCAA also found Ole Miss had failed to "dissociate" a booster in line with a 2017 infractions ruling. The university accepted about $109,000 and provided premium seating to the booster after the ruling.

Under a negotiated settlement, Ole Miss was required to end its relationship with the booster for two years, while athletic director Keith Carter and a senior official with the Ole Miss Athletic Foundation were required to attend an NCAA rules seminar.
